title: Resume Gaps? Say THIS Instead (The Quick Fix Recruiters Respect)
description:
Employment gaps aren’t the problem. Silence is.

When a resume doesn’t explain a career gap, employers often fill in the blanks themselves… and those assumptions are usually far worse than reality.

In this short, I show you a simple one-sentence fix you can add to your professional summary to explain a work gap clearly, professionally, and without oversharing.

If you’ve struggled with:
• employment gaps on your resume
• career breaks due to health or life changes
• getting ghosted after applying
• explaining gaps in interviews

…this strategy helps you stay credible, confident, and in control of your story.

transcript: Employers make up stories. If you're someone who has had a career gap and you don't give any context to that gap in your resume, sadly employers make up stories that are typically a lot worse than the actual scenario. To overcome this fast, you can simply put one swift sentence at the end of your professional summary. For example, if you had to leave the workforce due to a health reason, you could simply write a sentence saying, "Navigated a personal health journey from 2020 to 2021, returning with a renewed sense of resiliency and excitement to pursue professional endeavors."
